title: Planet Plastic
titleChinese: 地球快要变成“塑料星球”
paragraphs: Here‘s a staggering statistic. Scientists have calculated the total amount of plastic ever made: 8.3 billion tonnes. Looked at another way, that’s as heavy as 25,000 Empire State Buildings or one billion elephants. And incredibly, almost all of it has been made in the last 65 years.

So what‘s the problem? Much plastic is in the form of packaging which is used just once and then thrown away. According to a major new study from the University of California, 9% of this is recycled, 12% is incinerated and 79% goes to landfill. And because most plastic doesn’t biodegrade, once it‘s in the ground, it stays there.

It’s a situation that has led the paper‘s lead author, ecologist Dr Roland Geyer, to say that we are “rapidly heading towards ’Planet Plastic‘”. He believes that there’s already enough waste out there to cover the whole of Argentina.

The team behind this report also estimate that eight million tonnes of plastic waste are escaping into the sea every year. This has generated concern that plastic is entering the food chain, through fish and other sea life which ingest the smaller fragments.

Of course, the reason why there‘s so much plastic around is that it’s an amazingly useful material. We can‘t get enough of it. It’s durable and adaptable, and is used for everything from yoghurt pots to spaceships. But it‘s precisely this quality which makes it a problem. The only way to destroy plastic is to heat or burn it - although this has the side effect of harmful emissions.

So what’s the alternative, other than using less plastic? Oceanographer Dr Erik van Sebille from Utrecht University says we‘re facing a “tsunami” of plastic waste, and that the global waste industry needs to “get its act together”.

Professor Richard Thompson, a marine biologist from Plymouth University, says it’s poor design that‘s at fault. He says that if products are currently designed “with recyclability in mind”, they could be recycled around 20 times over.

Dr Geyer agrees: “The holy grail of recycling is to keep material in use and in the loop for ever if you can. But it turns out in our study that actually 90% of that material that did get recycled - which I think we calculated was 600 million tonnes - only got recycled once.”

vocabulary.entry: staggering [adj.] /ˈstæɡərɪŋ/ 惊人的；令人震惊的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The cost of the project was staggering.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的成本高得惊人。

vocabulary.entry: recycled [v.] /ˌriːˈsaɪkəld/ 回收利用；再利用 (原形: recycle)
vocabulary.example: Plastic bottles can be recycled into new products.
vocabulary.translation: 塑料瓶可以回收制成新产品。

vocabulary.entry: incinerated [v.] /ɪnˈsɪnəreɪtɪd/ 焚烧；焚毁 (原形: incinerate)
vocabulary.example: The waste was incinerated at a high temperature.
vocabulary.translation: 这些废物在高温下被焚烧。

vocabulary.entry: landfill [n.] /ˈlændfɪl/ 垃圾填埋场
vocabulary.example: Much of our rubbish ends up in landfill.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的大部分垃圾最终都进了垃圾填埋场。

vocabulary.entry: biodegrade [v.] /ˌbaɪəʊdɪˈɡreɪd/ 生物降解 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Unlike plastic, paper will biodegrade naturally.
vocabulary.translation: 与塑料不同，纸会自然生物降解。

vocabulary.entry: ingest [v.] /ɪnˈdʒest/ 摄入；摄取 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Sea creatures often ingest small pieces of plastic.
vocabulary.translation: 海洋生物常常摄入小块塑料。

vocabulary.entry: fragments [n. pl.] /ˈfræɡmənts/ 碎片；片段 (单数: fragment)
vocabulary.example: The vase broke into tiny fragments.
vocabulary.translation: 花瓶摔成了细小的碎片。

vocabulary.entry: durable [adj.] /ˈdjʊərəbəl/ 耐用的；持久的
vocabulary.example: This jacket is made of durable material.
vocabulary.translation: 这件夹克由耐用材料制成。

vocabulary.entry: emissions [n. pl.] /ɪˈmɪʃənz/ 排放物；散发物 (单数: emission)
vocabulary.example: Car emissions are a major cause of air pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 汽车尾气是空气污染的主要原因。

vocabulary.entry: holy grail [n.] /ˌhəʊli ˈɡreɪl/ 圣杯；梦寐以求的目标 (比喻)
vocabulary.example: Finding a cure for cancer is the holy grail of medical research.
vocabulary.translation: 找到癌症的治疗方法是医学研究的圣杯。

vocabulary.entry: ecologist [n.] /iːˈkɒlədʒɪst/ 生态学家 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Ecologists study the relationship between living things and their environment.
vocabulary.translation: 生态学家研究生物与其环境之间的关系。

vocabulary.entry: oceanographer [n.] /ˌəʊʃəˈnɒɡrəfə/ 海洋学家 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The oceanographer studies ocean currents and marine life.
vocabulary.translation: 这位海洋学家研究洋流和海洋生物。

vocabulary.entry: marine [adj.] /məˈriːn/ 海洋的；海产的
vocabulary.example: Marine life includes fish, whales, and coral.
vocabulary.translation: 海洋生物包括鱼类、鲸鱼和珊瑚。

vocabulary.entry: adaptable [adj.] /əˈdæptəbəl/ 适应性强；适应性好的
vocabulary.example: Plastic is a highly adaptable material.
vocabulary.translation: 塑料是一种适应性很强的材料。

vocabulary.entry: recyclability [n.] /ˌriːsaɪkləˈbɪləti/ 可回收性 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The recyclability of packaging is an important environmental consideration.
vocabulary.translation: 包装的可回收性是一个重要的环境考量因素。

vocabulary.entry: estimate [v.] /ˈestɪmeɪt/ 估计；估算
vocabulary.example: Experts estimate the damage at over $1 million.
vocabulary.translation: 专家估计损失超过100万美元。

vocabulary.entry: tsunami [n.] /tsuːˈnɑːmi/ 海啸；(比喻)浪潮
vocabulary.example: We are facing a tsunami of plastic waste.
vocabulary.translation: 我们正面临塑料垃圾的海啸。

vocabulary.entry: loop [n.] /luːp/ 循环；回路
vocabulary.example: The goal is to keep materials in a closed loop.
vocabulary.translation: 目标是让材料保持在闭环循环中。

vocabulary.entry: precisely [adv.] /prɪˈsaɪsli/ 精确地；恰好
vocabulary.example: It’s precisely because plastic is so useful that it has become a problem.
vocabulary.translation: 正是因为塑料如此有用，它才成了一个问题。

vocabulary.entry: generate [v.] /ˈdʒenəreɪt/ 产生；引起
vocabulary.example: The report has generated a lot of public interest.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告引起了公众的广泛兴趣。

sentences.english: Here‘s a staggering statistic.
sentences.chinese: 这里有一个惊人的统计数据。

sentences.english: Scientists have calculated the total amount of plastic ever made: 8.3 billion tonnes.
sentences.chinese: 科学家们计算出了有史以来生产的塑料总量：83亿吨。

sentences.english: Looked at another way, that’s as heavy as 25,000 Empire State Buildings or one billion elephants.
sentences.chinese: 换个角度看，这相当于25000座帝国大厦的重量，或者10亿头大象的重量。

sentences.english: And incredibly, almost all of it has been made in the last 65 years.
sentences.chinese: 令人难以置信的是，几乎所有这些塑料都是在过去65年里生产出来的。

sentences.english: So what‘s the problem?
sentences.chinese: 那么问题出在哪里呢？

sentences.english: Much plastic is in the form of packaging which is used just once and then thrown away.
sentences.chinese: 很多塑料是以包装的形式存在的，这些包装只使用一次就被扔掉了。

sentences.english: According to a major new study from the University of California, 9% of this is recycled, 12% is incinerated and 79% goes to landfill.
sentences.chinese: 根据加利福尼亚大学的一项重要新研究，其中9%的塑料被回收利用，12%被焚烧，79%被填埋到垃圾填埋场。

sentences.english: And because most plastic doesn’t biodegrade, once it‘s in the ground, it stays there.
sentences.chinese: 而且由于大多数塑料不会生物降解，一旦进入地下，就会一直留在那里。

sentences.english: It’s a situation that has led the paper‘s lead author, ecologist Dr Roland Geyer, to say that we are “rapidly heading towards ’Planet Plastic‘”.
sentences.chinese: 这种情况使得该论文的第一作者、生态学家罗兰·盖耶博士表示，我们正“迅速走向‘塑料星球’”。

sentences.english: He believes that there’s already enough waste out there to cover the whole of Argentina.
sentences.chinese: 他认为，现在已经有足够多的塑料垃圾可以覆盖整个阿根廷了。

sentences.english: The team behind this report also estimate that eight million tonnes of plastic waste are escaping into the sea every year.
sentences.chinese: 同时，这份报告背后的研究团队预估，每年有800万吨塑料垃圾流入海洋。

sentences.english: This has generated concern that plastic is entering the food chain, through fish and other sea life which ingest the smaller fragments.
sentences.chinese: 这引发了人们的担忧，担心塑料会通过摄入较小碎片的鱼类和其他海洋生物而进入食物链。

sentences.english: Of course, the reason why there‘s so much plastic around is that it’s an amazingly useful material.
sentences.chinese: 当然，有这么多塑料的原因是它是一种非常有用的材料。

sentences.english: We can‘t get enough of it.
sentences.chinese: 我们对它的需求源源不断。

sentences.english: It’s durable and adaptable, and is used for everything from yoghurt pots to spaceships.
sentences.chinese: 它耐用且适应性强，从酸奶罐到宇宙飞船，各种东西都要用到它。

sentences.english: But it‘s precisely this quality which makes it a problem.
sentences.chinese: 但恰好是这种特性使它成为了一个问题。

sentences.english: The only way to destroy plastic is to heat or burn it - although this has the side effect of harmful emissions.
sentences.chinese: 销毁塑料的唯一方法是加热或燃烧它——尽管这有产生有害排放物的副作用。

sentences.english: So what’s the alternative, other than using less plastic?
sentences.chinese: 那么，除了减少使用塑料之外，还有什么其他办法呢？

sentences.english: Oceanographer Dr Erik van Sebille from Utrecht University says we‘re facing a “tsunami” of plastic waste, and that the global waste industry needs to “get its act together”.
sentences.chinese: 乌得勒支大学的海洋学家埃里克·范·塞比尔博士说，我们正面临着塑料垃圾的“海啸”，全球垃圾处理行业需要“行动起来”。

sentences.english: Professor Richard Thompson, a marine biologist from Plymouth University, says it’s poor design that‘s at fault.
sentences.chinese: 普利茅斯大学的海洋生物学家理查德·汤普森教授说，设计不佳难辞其咎。

sentences.english: He says that if products are currently designed “with recyclability in mind”, they could be recycled around 20 times over.
sentences.chinese: 他说，如果目前的产品在设计时“考虑到可回收性”，它们可以被回收利用大约20次。

sentences.english: Dr Geyer agrees: “The holy grail of recycling is to keep material in use and in the loop for ever if you can.
sentences.chinese: 盖耶博士表示赞同：“回收利用的圣杯就是要尽可能让材料一直被使用并处于循环之中。

sentences.english: But it turns out in our study that actually 90% of that material that did get recycled - which I think we calculated was 600 million tonnes - only got recycled once.”
sentences.chinese: 但我们的研究表明，在我们计算得出约6亿吨的回收材料中，实际上90%的材料只被回收利用了一次而已。”
